selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveller believe was the main purpose of life in this world?
questions.answer: He believed the real purpose and core of life is faith.

questions.question: Why did the traveller want to look into the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He wanted to examine the book said to be the speech of the One they were seeking.

questions.question: How does the passage present the Qur'an’s challenge across time?
questions.answer: It says the challenge continues in every age, not only in the past.

questions.question: What shows that the traveller did not want to study carelessly?
questions.answer: He insisted on proving first that the Qur'an came from the Creator.

questions.question: What had to be settled before looking into the Qur'an’s teachings, according to the traveller?
questions.answer: It had to be settled that the Qur'an truly came from the Creator.

questions.question: What did the traveller examine first because he belonged to the present age?
questions.answer: He examined the Risale-i Nur first.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Risale-i Nur in an age of stubborn disbelief?
questions.answer: It says it spreads Qur'anic truths bravely and cannot be overcome.

questions.question: How many aspects of the Qur'an’s miraculous nature are said to be shown in one proof mentioned here?
questions.answer: Forty aspects.

questions.question: How are readers expected to react after seeing that proof?
questions.answer: They are expected to respect it and praise its reasoning rather than object to it.

questions.question: What did the traveller decide about presenting all those proofs himself?
questions.answer: He decided not to present all of them there and instead to mention only a few signs of the Qur'an’s greatness.

questions.question: Who was the traveller speaking to at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: He was speaking to his own heart.

questions.question: What two things did he want to learn about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He wanted to know what it says and whether it truly comes from the Creator.

questions.question: Whose speech was the Qur'an said to be?
questions.answer: It was said to be the speech of the Being the traveller was seeking.

questions.question: What ongoing feature of the Qur'an is highlighted in the passage?
questions.answer: Its challenge continues through every age.

questions.question: What was the traveller’s first goal before studying the Qur'an’s message?
questions.answer: His first goal was to establish that it is from the Creator.

questions.question: How are the parts of the Risale-i Nur described?
questions.answer: They are described as many sections that present bright insights and solid explanations taken from the Qur'an.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that no one can defeat the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It suggests that the truth it carries is powerful and that its source is divine, not man-made.

questions.question: What is special about the proof found in the two named sections of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It explains many sides of the Qur'an’s miraculous character in a powerful way.

questions.question: What do the named sections of the Risale-i Nur accomplish regarding the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They show many dimensions of its miraculous nature.

questions.question: In the end, what approach did the traveller take in this passage?
questions.answer: He relied on the Risale-i Nur for the full case and gave only a short introduction to a few points about the Qur'an’s greatness.

questions.question: According to him, what gives life its true meaning?
questions.answer: Faith gives life its true meaning.

questions.question: What was the name used in the passage for the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It was called the Qur'an of Miraculous Exposition.

questions.question: What claim is made about the Qur'an compared with other books?
questions.answer: It is presented as the most famous, radiant, and wise book.

questions.question: What is said about the proof found in the Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter?
questions.answer: It presents forty strong signs of the Qur'an’s miraculous quality.
